featured_reviews.name: Omkar Nadkarni
featured_reviews.review_text: Dr Henna and her staff are one of the most supportive vets (and I'll speak for my pets too) in the city. I see the staff connecting with the animals to gain their trust before any procedure. I'd strongly recommend Critter Care to any and all pet lovers!

featured_reviews.name: Viraal Trivedi
featured_reviews.review_text: The worst experience ever! Lost one of my budgies due to anaesthesia reaction. Despite informing them about it, they went ahead and compulsorily went for x-ray and blood test under sedation! All they had to do was just trim his nails because at home they don’t get those natural ways to trim themselves. They were treating my other budgie for liver issues whereas the real concern was hormonal. They don’t know anything on how to handle cases. Would never go and would never recommend this one to anybody
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
All our patients mean alot to us. Losing any one is devastating. We're sorry for your loss. 
Taking x-rays and blood under sedation is high standard of care as per world standards. Doing so without is stressful for the patient. Anesthestic risk is unfortunate and sometimes unpredictable. That being said, we cannot force anyone into doing diagnostics. It is a choice.
We hope Yelly is healthy and happy and continues to be so.
Take care and wish you all the best.

featured_reviews.name: Ashna Srivastava
featured_reviews.review_text:
I cannot express enough gratitude for the exceptional care my dog Tara received at Critter Care Veterinarian Clinic. Dr. Henna, Dr. Faye, Dr. Nidhi, Dr. Bhushan and the entire team went above and beyond to ensure Tara's well-being. During our first visit, they swiftly diagnosed her with TVT cancer, providing clarity and a comprehensive plan moving forward. The team at Critter Care supported us every step of the way, ensuring Tara received the treatment she needed to overcome her illness. Their dedication and hard work paid off - Tara is now cancer-free!

Even during clinic renovations, they seamlessly arranged alternative care for Tara, showcasing their unwavering commitment. I am forever grateful to the doctors at Critter Care for their compassion and expertise. Kudos to this remarkable team for their outstanding service and saving Tara's life.

featured_reviews.name: Rachel Atwood
featured_reviews.review_text: I went here because it's one of the few places that takes care of rabbits. However, I stopped taking our pet rabbit here because they weren't super responsive for issues when I wasn't physically on property with the animal. The first visit was great, and I was super happy. However, after that, the only response I'd get was: send a stool sample, with no context or information to help me understand if what I was seeing was a huge issue or nothing to worry about. After the second time they asked for that, I turned to Google and Google was way more helpful: the issue was the result of a change in diet, which they should have known considering it was their instructions that caused the change in diet (i.e. it wasn't something to worry about). Basically I got the impression that the goal was to make money only. Fine, it's a business, they should make money, but not at the expense of ensuring care for the critters they see.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
We're sorry you feel this way. We do prefer to talk over the phone or face to face rather than on text especially when we're working with patients all day and can't be texting. 
We run diagnostics to rule out any serious issues because we care for our patients and want to do what's right by them. Prevention will cost way less than treating a horrific medical condition.
Feel free to come and speak to us at the clinic or call us to talk about any issues. If only Google could do our job, we wouldn't need to study and work so hard. 
Take care.

featured_reviews.name: Shaivika Chandekar
featured_reviews.review_text: The prices they charge are very high. For simple consultation they charged me Rs 800 and for a normal heath certificate Rs.1000 where they did not even touch my cat for any kind of check-up. The certificate was also not given by Dr. Henna but rather some other junior doctor. The medicine the use are of good quality but they need to work around what they are charging.

featured_reviews.name: Pratik Shah
featured_reviews.review_text: Bad experience. The doctor lacks empathy. Does not pick up phone early in the morning or respond to messages. Neither at night. So if it's an emergency, you're left on your own. By the time her staff finds time to call you late during the day, your pet would have passed away. Happened to me with two of my pets, both of which were treated and advised okay to be taken home by her. In spite of which they passed away. No, the doctor didn't have the courtesy to call back and enquire, even if the pet she was treating, died.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hi Pratik. Could you please give us more details about your pets? We can't seem to find you on our system.
Unfortunately we are not a 24 hour clinic and try to fit in as many patients as we can during working hours. There are 24 hour emergency clinics that would be able to help you at night, we're currently not equipped to do so.
If you give us further details, we can help figure out what went wrong.

I was in a panic because she was already so stressed from the flight and the moving as we didn’t have our familiar surroundings and our family vet as in USA .

featured_reviews.name: Natasha Pink
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dr. Akshay 😇 I can’t find words to describe this man! Such words have not yet been invented in any language! My story is 7 months long.
On April 6, one of my children all got sick at once, 6 puppies near my house. I urgently flew from Mumbai home to Varanasi, what I saw tore my heart into small pieces! They were paralyzed! I realized that this was a nervous plague. But I have never encountered this before, I don’t know how to treat it, and the most annoying thing is that we don’t have doctors in Varanasi who would be so professional. It was hell. Between changing diapers and calming the children, in tears, I read veterinary forums and literature. I called hundreds of veterinarians in Russia. And most of them recommended euthanization. I just can’t explain to the Russian people that according to our religion, we cannot take anyone’s life. I tried... I tried everything! Everything I could! We even got the serum delivered from Mumbai. I went to a human medical school, but out of desperation, I learned how to give IVs to dogs. Nobody wants to help me, everyone shrugged their shoulders, but I was simply dying from pain and hopelessness. I prayed day and night for Shiva and Ganesha to decide and either take them away or for them to go to recovery. Day after day, week after week, month after month. I did massages and continued to fight the plague. The children died in my arms, and by lowering them into the Ganges, I also lowered part of my heart. Of all the people, only Snezhana was able to defeat the plague! But she also remained bedridden. Bedsores, heart and kidney failure, then diarrhea and constipation began. The only thing that remained unchanged was his excellent appetite.How many tears I shed is known only to the gods. And the day came when my visa expired.... I took Snezhana to animal Rescue....
And I thought that I would never see her again. In Rescue, no one had time for massages and her bedsores became bone-chip. I was dying sitting in Russia, on my knees at the consulate so that they would quickly check my documents. But they kept dragging on (they were embarrassed by my appearance, although I offered to put me on a polygraph and they were convinced that I had never used anything), at that moment they found a tumor on my dad, and it just pulled me to the window, just to jump and not suffer anymore. But I continued to pray and Ganesha brought me a Russian guy who agreed to watch Snezhana and do a massage. I rented them a room in the house where Snezhana was born (my room is also there). But he didn’t have enough energy for a massage. Her paws became like those of a female praying mantis. I watched the video every day and lost hope.... Until Ganesh Chaturthi came! A Pandit from India came to Moscow, I went to pray, we got into a conversation and he asked, “During the yagya, was it uncomfortable for you to sit?”, I told him my story of a spinal fracture and how I stood up thanks to Ganesha and also mentioned that acupuncture helped me a lot!
The text continues in the photo, the whole story didn't fit.

featured_reviews.name: Minal Mankar
featured_reviews.review_text:
About 3 months ago, our 3-month-old puppy Mylo swallowed a large mutton bone from the trash. An initial X-ray at another hospital showed it was stuck in his throat near the neck. He was vomiting and not eating anything, and as time passed, he started breathing strangely, almost as if he was choking. We were extremely worried.

Through a common friend, we connected with Dr. Gaurav at Suyash Pet Clinic, Chembur. Even before we visited, he stayed in constant touch over the phone and guided us calmly. At the clinic, he immediately attended to Mylo, started him on saline, and did another X-ray. He clearly explained the situation, the size of the bone, the endoscopy procedure, and all associated risks, while also reassuring us throughout.

What truly stood out was his patience, kindness, and genuine care—not just for Mylo, but for us as anxious pet parents. He did everything he could to avoid surgery, and thankfully, the endoscopy was successful. Mylo recovered well, and we couldn’t be more grateful.

We had visited another hospital before this and felt very unsure due to their lack of clarity and significantly higher costs. In such emergencies, having a doctor who is both skilled and empathetic is truly a blessing.

Highly recommend Suyash Pet Clinic and Dr. Gaurav without hesitation. Writing this review after 2+ months, with a happy and healthy Mylo ❤️
